memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: "If, however, they are poor and cannot afford these offerings, they must take one male lamb as a guilt offering to be waved to make atonement for them, together with a tenth of an ephah of the finest flour mixed with olive oil for a grain offering, a log of oil, and two doves or two young pigeons, such as they can afford, one for a sin offering and the other for a burnt offering." - Lev 14:21-22 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
Such as they can afford. Four words that reveal the heart of God.

He has just laid out an expensive ceremony — three lambs and generous quantities of flour and oil. And immediately He makes provision for the person who cannot possibly manage it. The requirement drops. The result does not.

Think about who this is for. Someone who has been outside the camp for months, unable to earn, unable to farm, dependent on others. The poorest person in Israel. God writes them into the law by name.

This is not a God who has one door for the wealthy and a side entrance for everyone else. Note carefully what does not change: the guilt offering lamb remains. Atonement still requires blood. God does not lower the truth to accommodate poverty — He carries the cost differently so the poor can come.

And this is where the whole Bible has been heading. Not one of us could afford our own cleansing, rich or poor. So God provided the offering Himself. Come, all you who are thirsty, come to the waters; and you who have no money, come, buy and eat! (Isa 55:1).

Whatever you have or do not have, the door is open to you.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. Have you ever felt you had too little to bring to God?
2. Does your church make it as easy for the poor to belong as the comfortable?
3. What does God's provision for the poor tell you about His character?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Father, thank You that Your grace has never been priced beyond anyone's reach. Thank You for providing what I could never afford, and make me generous towards those with less. Amen.
